 This petition coming on for admission this day, the court passed the
following:
 Order

This petition under Article 227 of Constitution of India has been filed seeking the following reliefs:-
"(i) That this Hon'ble Court may kindly be pleased to issue writ in the nature of certiorari and set aside the entire proceeding of the trial court in MJC No. 19/2012 (Anuradha Verma Vs. Amit Verma & others) pending before judicial Magistrate First Class, Sagar, District Sagar.

(ii) Any other relief which this Hon'ble Court may kindly be deemed fit and proper in favor of petitioner may also be given together with cost of petition, in the interest of justice."
2.
It is the case of petitioners that respondent is the daughter-in-law of petitioner Nos. 1 and 2 and wife of petitioner No. 4, whereas; petitioner No. 3 is the brother-in-law of respondent.

It is submitted by counsel for petitioners that on the report lodged by respondent an offence under Sections 498-A, 406 of IPC read with Section 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act was registered and ultimately they were acquitted by trial Court by judgment dated 12.10.2018.
The appeal filed by respondent against the acquittal of petitioners has also been dismissed by order dated 14.08.2019.

sentences.text: The respondent had also filed a complaint under Section 12 of Domestic Violence Act with a malafide intention by making false allegations against petitioners.
The said case was registered as MJC No. 19/2012.
During the pendency of trial, petitioners moved an application for discharge which was dismissed by order dated 14.07.2015.
Against the said order, petitioners preferred Criminal Appeal 323/2015 before the Appellate Court which was also dismissed by Appellate Court.
3. Thereafter, the petitioners filed M.Cr.C. No. 10154/2017 for quashment of entire proceeding without seeking of quashment of order mentioned above.

Initially in the said application an interim order was passed by this Court by order dated 04.07.2017 but later on, the M.Cr.C. was dismissed as not maintainable by order dated 30.11.2023 with liberty to petitioners to file Miscellaneous Petition under Article 227 of Constitution of India.

Thereafter, petitioners filed M.P. No. 7509/2023,
however, because of certain inherent defects, the same was withdrawn with liberty to file a fresh Miscellaneous Petition.
Accordingly, this petition has been filed.

4. It is submitted by counsel for petitioners that once petitioners have been acquitted for offence under Sections 498-A, 406 of IPC and Section 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, the complaint under Section 12 of Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act is not maintainable.

entities.text: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: It is further submitted that the complaint made by respondent is barred by limitation as provided under Section 468 of Cr.P.C. because the limitation is one year, whereas; the complaint was filed after several years.
5. Heard learned counsel for petitioners.
6. Under the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, no provision is penal in nature except Section 31 of Act.

entities.text: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
7. Section 31 of Act reads as under:-
"31. Penalty for breach of protection order by respondent.--(1) A breach of protection order, or of an interim protection order, by the respondent shall be an offence under this Act and shall be punishable with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to twenty thousand rupees, or with both.
(2) The offence under sub-section (1) shall as far as practicable be tried by the Magistrate who had passed the order, the breach of which has been alleged to have been caused by the accused.
(3) While framing charges under sub-section (1), the Magistrate may also frame charges under section 498A of the Indian Penal Code (45 of 1860) or any other provision of that Code or the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 (28 of 1961), as the case may be, if the facts disclose the commission of an offence under those provisions."

sentences.text: Thus, the question of punishment would arise only if the order of protection is violated.
No period of limitation has been provided for filing an application under Section 12 of Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act.

sentences.text:
Further by making an application under Section 12 of Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act the aggrieved person can pray for right to reside in a shared household, can ask for protection orders, can ask for residence orders, can ask for monetary reliefs,
can ask for custody orders and can also ask for compensation.

sentences.text: Merely because petitioners have been acquitted for offence under Section 498-A of IPC would not debar the complainant/agreed person for seeking the aforementioned relief(s) as provided under Sections 17 to 22 of the Act.

9. Therefore, in considered opinion of this Court, the mere acquittal of petitioners for offence under Sections 498-A, 406 of IPC and Section 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act would not ipso facto make the application filed under Section 12 of Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act not maintainable.

entities.text: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 10. So far as the question of limitation is concerned, it appears that the complaint was filed on 02.05.2012.
As already pointed out, there is no penal provision under the Act 2005 except Section 31 of Act.
11. Since, no protection order has been issued so far, therefore, no application under Section 31 of Act, 2005 can be filed at this stage.
12. Whether the provision of Section 468 of Cr.P.C.

would apply to the proceedings under Section 31 of Act, 2005 is not under consideration but one thing is clear that since no other penal provision is provided under the Act, 2005, therefore, the provision of Section 468 of Cr.P.C. would not apply.

13. Considering the totality of the facts and circumstances of the case, this Court is of the considered opinion that no case is made out warranting interference in the complaint filed by respondent under Section 12 of Act, 2005.
14 . Accordingly, petition fails and is hereby dismissed.
